result:
Quick correction before anything else: that's not quite right. A language model call is stateless — each time you call it, it only "knows" what's in the text you send it that time, plus whatever it learned during training. It doesn't keep anything between calls on its own.

Concrete example: when you chat with something like ChatGPT and it seems to remember what you said five messages ago, that's because the app is quietly resending your whole conversation so far as part of the text it gives the model each turn. Close the chat and the model has no trace of it — the appearance of memory was the app's doing, not the model's.

So for your makerspace assistant: if a student told it something last week, the model itself won't recall that next week. Your team has to build that — save what matters (say, to a file or database), then pull the relevant bit back out and paste it into the text you send the model next time the student shows up. That's exactly the "what does the assistant save between sessions" piece in your mission — it's an engineering decision you make, not something the model gives you for free.

Quick check: if a student tells the assistant "I finished my laser cutter training" today, and comes back tomorrow asking to book the laser cutter, what has to happen in between for the assistant to know they're trained?
